subject: Proposal: carry-forward credit + staggered uplift to co-term
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen@wandr.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-cycle capacity uplift — options & procurement constraints

Hi Vanessa,

We’re seeing a material usage uptick for our customer-facing agents and need to increase committed capacity from 10M token-equivalents/mo to ~15M starting immediately. Renewal is currently Jan 15, 2027 and procurement wants to avoid multiple full invoices between now and renewal.

Two specific asks from procurement:
- Can Redwood provide an option to apply any pro-rated overage/one-time payment as a carry-forward credit toward the Jan 2027 renewal?
- If not, can we amortize the uplift over X invoices (they suggested 3) instead of a single up-front invoice?

I’ve attached our last 90-day usage export to help size the uplift. We’re also open to a short-term discount if we annualize the added capacity now and co-term to Jan.

Can you outline 2–3 commercial options (pro-rate, carry-forward credit, staggered co-term) and any lead-time or contract language changes we should expect?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Best,
Helen Park
Head of AI Ops, Wandr AI
Attachments: Wandr-usage-report.csv (csv)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen@wandr.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity uplift — options & procurement constraints

Hi Helen,

Thanks for the usage export — that helps a lot. We can absolutely support the three paths you outlined. Below are practical options with trade-offs and a recommended path given you want minimal billing friction before Jan 15: 

1) One-time uplift (pro-rated) — quickest to implement- Description: Increase committed capacity to 15M token-eq/mo immediately; invoice pro-rated for remainder of the current billing period.- Pricing: +5% unit discount on incremental capacity for the remainder of the contract term.- Contract impact: standard mid-term amendment; no co-term change.

2) Carry-forward credit (recommended if procurement dislikes up-front invoices)- Description: We invoice the uplift now, but any unused portion of the uplift (calculated monthly) becomes a credit that rolls into the Jan 15 renewal and can be applied against the first 6 months of usage under the renewed commitment.- Pricing: +3% unit discount on incremental capacity if you accept carry-forward that applies only at renewal (better immediate cash flow for you).- Contract impact: amendment + renewal schedule noting credit mechanics and expiration.

3) Staggered co-term / amortized billing- Description: Annualize the uplift now and co-term to Jan 15, 2027; total uplift amount is split across 3 invoices (amortized) leading up to renewal.- Pricing: +8% unit discount on incremental capacity vs one-off (incentive for annualization).- Contract impact: requires co-term amendment and a simple payment schedule; procurement must agree to the staged invoice plan.

Additional concession: Karthik has confirmed we can offer a one-time migration/onboarding credit (I’ll let him propose the exact amount if you prefer annualization). I’ve attached a short proposed amendment that models options 2 and 3 and includes the carry-forward clause language we typically use.

Next steps: if you prefer option 2 or 3 I can send a clean/redline and open a DocuSign. If procurement needs the amortization mechanics formalized (specific invoice dates/amounts), send me the procurement contact and we’ll draft the schedule they can sign off on.

If helpful, I’m available for a 20m call tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Attachments: Proposed_Amendment_20260917.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Helen Park <helen@wandr.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity uplift — options & procurement constraints

Quick note from me — I reviewed Vanessa’s options and approved a one-time $5,000 onboarding credit we can apply if Wandr annualizes the uplift now and co-terms to Jan 15.

We see this as a reasonable trade for predictability (and it helps offset migration cost for you). If Helen/procurement wants the onboarding credit included in the amendment, Vanesssa, please add a short clause calling it out and the conditions (annualize + sign within 10 business days).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: Helen Park <helen@wandr.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Wandr AI Procurement <procurement@wandr.ai>
Date: 2026-09-19T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity uplift — options & procurement constraints

Vanessa — thanks, that framing is helpful. Procurement reviewed the three options and here’s where we landed: 

- We prefer option 3 (staggered co-term / amortized billing) but need the staged invoices to be explicit (dates and amounts). Procurement will accept 3 invoices: Oct 15, Nov 15, Dec 15 splitting the uplift equally.
- The $5k onboarding credit is fine — procurement requests it be captured as a one-time credit line item in the amendment.
- Two must-have edits to the amendment: remove the auto-renew clause (procurement cannot accept automatic renewal without a manual renewal trigger) and add language that the carry-forward credit (if any unused) must expire no earlier than 6 months after co-term.

If you can send a redline that includes the invoice dates and both edits, procurement will route it for signature the same day. Also copying our procurement lead (procurement@wandr.ai) for any legal-specific notes.

On timing — we can sign the amendment by Sep 24 if the redline is sent by Sep 21.

Thanks — happy to sign once those two edits are in.

Best,
Helen Park
Head of AI Ops, Wandr AI
